would_have_shipped_defects.evidence: artefacts/scripts/hive-score:217-221 (parse_predictions called only when ORDER_REL is non-empty) vs artefacts/scripts/hive-score:237 `if [ -n "$PRED_EFFORT_TXT" ]`, with `set -euo pipefail` inherited from artefacts/scripts/hive-common.sh:26; candidate.patch:216-227 and 235-243 show the previously unconditional initialisations being deleted. Reproduced in isolation: `PRED_EFFORT_TXT: unbound variable`, exit=1. verifier/metrics-drill.log contains no no-order-file scoring case.
would_have_shipped_defects.summary: Refactoring the prediction regexes into `parse_predictions` left `PRED_EFFORT_TXT`/`PRED_QUESTIONS_TXT`/`PRED_REVIEW_TXT` unset on the no-order-file path, so `hive-score` now aborts with `unbound variable` under `set -u` instead of scoring the task as unpredicted.
would_have_shipped_defects.why_blocking: Before this patch the three `PRED_*_TXT=$( ... )` assignments ran unconditionally, so a closed task with no order file scored cleanly as unpredicted — a path hive-score's own header calls "a legitimate outcome (the 2026-07-13 hand-seeded task ids do not invert to their filenames, and never will)" and "a real, and interesting, case". After the patch they are assigned only inside `parse_predictions`, which is called only in the `[ -n "$ORDER_REL" ]` branch. The operator running `hive-score <hand-seeded-task> --project omegahive` now gets a raw bash error and exit 1 with no calibration entry written; the sibling `PREDICTIONS_SECTION` reference on line 283 was defensively written as `${PREDICTIONS_SECTION:-0}`, so the omission is inconsistent rather than deliberate. The 106-check metrics drill has no fixture for a closed task without an order file, so it is green with the regression live.

would_have_shipped_defects.evidence: candidate.patch touches exactly five files — scripts/hive-close, scripts/hive-common.sh, scripts/hive-launch, scripts/hive-metrics-drill.sh, scripts/hive-score (candidate.patch:1,26,91,127,193). No RUNBOOK, reports/ or result-report content appears anywhere in the patch or in artefacts/, which holds only the three scripts.
would_have_shipped_defects.summary: The order's non-code deliverables are entirely absent: no result report (What shipped / How verified / To operate / Reflection) and no RUNBOOK update.
would_have_shipped_defects.why_blocking: DoD requires a result report filed under the project's reports directory, and the rubric grades it explicitly (it lists only the spine *announcement* as out of reach, stating "The report the order asks for IS written and graded"). DoD (i) additionally requires RUNBOOK updates where the operator surface changed, and three surfaces did change: the new launch refusal plus `--anyway` escape hatch, `hive-close` now regenerating metrics, and the `--review` vocabulary. The order also requires the report's "To operate" to name the recovery step `hive-score <task> --project pln-benchmarks --again` for the two lost pln calibration data points; with no report, that recovery instruction is nowhere. An operator hitting the new launch refusal has no documented path, and the two lost calibration points are never recovered.
